reviews.text: Drawn from a short story by the author of Cat Person, Halina Reijn’s English-language debut is refreshingly uninterested in female bodily gore.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: Not only does director Halina Reijn get in a ton of laughs as well as a ton of drama and thrills, but her film takes the murder-mystery premise and turns it on its head in a way a lot of people might not see coming.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: …that the final twist redeems this entire film is unusual and admirable; what’s missing here is the engagement and disguise that might have made Bodies Bodies Bodies worth sitting through to appreciate the pay-off…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: In her controlled English-language debut, Dutch filmmaker Reijn ... uses genre to expose, not without affection, a generation steeped in youth, sex and power — or at least the appearance of it — and how that wreaks havoc on sincere, honest relationships.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Director Halina Reijn's critique set in a post-truth world is self-aware, understands its target audience very well, and does everything to cater to them.
reviews.author: Tamma Moksha

reviews.text: For those who don’t fully appreciate its distinct brand of humor, there’s still enough of a twisty, turny good time to make it worthwhile, although the charm wanes fairly quickly.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Stripped of the group chats and podcasts, the Twitter and TikTok that define them, these young people are confronted with their unmediated selves, and no one will come out looking pretty.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: Not for me, clever in some ways and great performances
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Put a group of wealthy, narcissistic Gen Z friends in a large, remote estate filled with drugs and staircases in the middle of a hurricane and see what your outcome is.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Although some of the jokes attached to the script might not hit in full force as much as the writers tended to, the rest uplifts it, making it a worthwhile bloody good time.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Hilariously well acted and a breath of fresh air into the horror genre, Bodies Bodies Bodies is full of Gen Z humour, fake friends, blood, tears and bad decisions.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a fun dark comedy that works as a slasher, social satire, and even as a whodunit where no one is who they seem. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carla Monfort

reviews.text: ... In general the film crackles with life. It has a caustic script, a stormy atmosphere and a talented cast.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: One of 2022's 20 best films.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: ... Tries to be in tune with the times of political correctness, feminist empowerment, and sexual fluidity, but ultimately ends up settling on a classic structure -- a wild party that ends in bloody bacchanalia. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: ... A mortal show that combines crime, terror, and comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Monserrat

reviews.text: A cringey, yet crucial, part of the Gen Z cinematic universe.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: The plot isn't particularly amusing, the kills aren't at all interesting, and the point appears to be the pointlessness... the Thelma and Louise of whodunnit plot devices... if you can't take the yeet, get out of the mansion.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Established the next era of slashers.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: A24’s horror flick brought together some of the best Gen Z performers, from Rachel Sennott to Amandla Stenberg—alongside Pete Davidson—but Wonders was the clear breakthrough performer.
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: Whodunnits are back with a vengeance. This inspired slasher twist boasts a thrilling satirical energy and a sizzling Gen Z cast, including Amandla Stenberg and Borat’s Maria Bakalova.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Watching them try to cope with this unfolding And Then There We None set-up is like watching The Lord of the Flies populated by a cast of narcissistic incompetents.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Additional depths may be absent, but who can argue with a landing that sticks so damn well?
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: In true Agatha Christie fashion, the trust-fund guests are all suspects and probably next. A riot, the final reveal is deliciously wicked.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Initially, Bodies Bodies Bodies seems content to be a less stylish take on Spring Breakers. But then, it deviates from what looks like a standard horny and drug addled young adult debauchery escapade into something far more entertaining.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies offers a surprising amount of fun with its dark humor and razor sharp wit. The performances are engaging, the location is claustrophobic, and it has a killer twist that will catch you by surprise.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Halina Reijn's 'Bodies Bodies Bodies' is one of the most satisfying and funny slasher thrillers you will see this year.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: A whodunnit that feels like Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring had a baby, then had Agatha Christie’s And Then There Were None as its nanny.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: With a frightfully fun cast, a tight script, and a thematically relevant approach to its violence, Bodies Bodies Bodies is great slasher fun.
reviews.author: Diego Peralta

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies evinces a lot of responses, but it made me want to give a Zoomer a hug if needed and rides to the airport when asked.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: A hilarious and gripping whodunit with sharp dialogue that puts a fresh spin on the conventional slasher formula. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: A deliriously silly and entertaining slasher-cum-whodunit in the Scream tradition
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: With a killer cast [...] the film is cleverly written with an twisted and unexpected answer to who really dunnit.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: By juxtaposing this current, politically correct terminology with  the very real threat of impending doom as the characters are massacred one by one, DeLappe slyly critiques pop culture by presenting these terms in life or death circumstances.
reviews.author: Katherine Powell

reviews.text: A Zillennial scorcher of a comedy that hoovers up a little too much blow and crashes its Beemer into an old-school whodunit.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The spirit of Wes Craven’s Scream is obviously visible, as is the mischievousness of unsung slashers like Fred Walton’s April Fools Day, all through the ultra modern torch light of the latest iPhone!
reviews.author: Jack Bottomley

reviews.text: While not an entirely memorable take on the whodunnit genre, Bodies remains darkly funny and enjoyable.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: This feels like hanging out with the worst possible group, but still loving it somehow - a twisted and hilarious delight.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The movie is never funny, scary, spooky, or interesting.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is an extremely fun time that blends tried-and-true genre tropes of a whodunnit with prescient views on the human condition in a story that is funny, thrilling and simmering with angst that is sure to provoke.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The problematic phrase “guilty pleasure” will just about do for Halina Reijn’s Bodies Bodies Bodies, the kind of horror parody so edgy it practically slices and dices itself.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Fun fun fun and very well done.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Hilarious, ridiculous, brutal and satisfying... [a] romp of a slasher-comedy.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: … a film that would have probably worked better as a series of TikToks.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is pretty funny, and misses no opportunity to take cheap swipes at the poor millennials, who are an easy target. This film is fonder of itself that might be seemly, but it’s also a lot of fun.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Fun, brutal and thoroughly entertaining, this modern slasher is well worth your time. Come for the gory kills, stay for the thoughtful and shocking exploration of human nature.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: By the end, I was fond of every single brat, dead or alive.
reviews.author: Nick James

reviews.text: A bitingly funny satire of Gen Z. You may walk out asking what the point of it all was, but that's, well, the point.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: The fun, of course, is in the pillory, yet the (deliberately) loathsome nature of the characters soon becomes draining.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The killings aren’t especially scary but there’s sharp dialogue as the self-obsessed youths go at each other with psycho-babble buzzwords including “gas lighting” and “triggering”.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: It’s peak nihilistic entertainment, watching these souls try, in vain, to keep their fragile reputations intact while they’re drenched head to toe in blood.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The title could hint at either sex or death, and both end up with roles to play in a movie carefully stuffed with rising stars du jour.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Reijn’s finely orchestrated ambience of frenzy and tension is a blast to watch, and the game performances, particularly from the young ensemble cast of female actors as they savagely jump at each other’s throats, deliciously ups the ante.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: A little over-eager in hitting all of its slightly banal cultural touchstones.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Its status as a social media metaphor is perfectly integrated into a gory, funny, fiendishly clever plot with an audaciously outré twist-ending to boot.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It’s easy to laugh at Gen Z. But they deserve something a whole lot sharper than this.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies cements itself as an outrageous satirical look at a chaotic, quick-moving generation, serving as the definitive depiction of Generation Z in entertainment.
reviews.author: Diego Andaluz

reviews.text: A smart and cynical dark comedy about the fleeting nature of friends and lovers. While the humour could be said to target Twitter and Gen Z, the satire is pretty universal. These people ain't pretty
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: One of the year's laziest films.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: All drugs and no cell-service make these party-revellers very dangerous indeed in this wickedly funny and devilishly frightening tale of toxic friendships.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: There is something horrifically and fantastically over the top about Bodies Bodies Bodies that makes it so delightful to watch.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: Reduced to its miserable insignificance, Bodies Bodies Bodies is instantly forgotten.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: A compelling slasher genre re-invigoration.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: This is stunningly bad.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: A frenetic, bloody satire of aimless, wealthy, overeducated youth.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: It's a delightfully modern, dark-humored whodunit.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Like so many horror films attempting to be subversive, Bodies Bodies Bodies tries to satirize the upper class. But all it delivers are tired, lazy tropes about Gen Z.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Reijn’s avant-garde style is striking and the layered characters are full of intrigue, but we never really get to know them -- and the lack of clues as to the culprit turns a whodunit into a less interesting game of Guess Who?
reviews.author: Ray Gill Jr.

reviews.text: The cast is game and Reijn is happy to let their characters shed their humanity with ease. And while the reveal is obvious, its hilarious predictability renders it perfect, nonetheless.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A smart satire about bored, rich kids who only feel happy when they think they're being victimized.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The movie's strong finish can’t quite compensate for the sluggish set-up...
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is the latest movie so eager to crack the pathology of the youths that it loses the texture of actual teenage behavior.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: It’s a credit to Reijn’s skill that she navigates the film to that climax despite the rough waters at the start of the voyage, and like some English guy said once upon a time, all’s well that ends well.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: This should have been more fun watching… it was just annoying.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: One of the most searing indictments of the social media age and its effects on young people I’ve ever seen.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: It’s a very solid, socially relevant horror comedy, but I needed more horror and comedy to support the ideas at play, or make them stick more. Also, good for Connor O’Malley.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Director Halina Reijn, working from a screenplay by Sarah DeLappe, has crafted a fun hybrid that uses elements of a thriller to serve as an acidic social satire that captures the angst of Generation Z.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is an aesthetically-pleasing slasher filled with witty dialogue and unlikable characters. However, the lack of layers and character development will leave you wanting more.
reviews.author: Justin Carreiro

reviews.text: In a way, Bodies Bodies Bodies, like its title, is little more than a cinematic game -- but its well-played by a strong young cast that gives the movie plenty of zing.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Summer blockbuster season is definitely over when this toxic kind of horror/slasher trash worms its way into local theaters.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies takes a satirical jab at the attitudes and discourse of Generation Z by pitting insufferable characters against growing paranoia. Unfortunately, the movie achieved it's goal too well and my enjoyment factor didn't survive the toxicity
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: The genius of Sarah DeLappe's screenplay... is that the penultimate revelation brilliantly incorporates the handheld tech on which these characters depend. It's a conclusion that is as hilarious as it is horrifying.
reviews.author: Gregg Shapiro

reviews.text: Tense when it needs to be and awfully good fun throughout. Stupidity reigns supreme for these rich kids, but the filmmakers are smart enough to make Bodies Bodies Bodies stick the landing.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: At a crisply paced 95 minutes, Bodies Bodies Bodies is a satisfying cinematic snack.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: It’s like one of those Date Movie type spoofs where you’re just supposed to laugh because you recognize the reference.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: I liked it, can't say that I loved it.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: "[Its] satire isn't as sharp as the killer's weapon."
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Though it can drag a bit in the middle and a few of the jokes fall flat, the final punchline so thoroughly kills that it largely absolves it of its prior missteps.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Offers an enjoyable (and perceptive) murderous killer story that feels familiar, yet different. It’s psychological horror with a body count.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Two sequences encapsulate the best and worst of a film that cleverly upends the slasher genre while trying to desperately sell too late the word salad of a me-generation obsessed with appearing philanthropic while destroying things around them.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: The script is ultimately heavy-handed in its needling of ultra-rich young people, but a solid cast grounds the characters in specifics, breathing life into the noxious dynamics that permeate the crew and unsettle from the start.
reviews.author: Kayla Kumari Upadhyaya

reviews.text: The dialog is witty and quick, with some bite to it and moments of pointed social commentary. The dark comedy works well and the actors effectively create an ominous tone of mistrust that permeates the story.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: With perhaps one lone exception, these characters aren’t meant to be liked. But we should be able to tolerate them which I found to be harder and harder as the story went on.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a wicked and bloody good time.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is filled with great dialogue, an intriguing plot, and social commentary that will surely make for fantastic conversation.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: However you read it, the movie is dynamic, ruthless, occasionally bloody, very funny, and something decidedly enjoyable...
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: With an all-star cast of young and talented actors, nervous laughs, and violent slashes, Bodies Bodies Bodies is easily one of the most exciting movies of 2022.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: While Bodies Bodies Bodies might have had the potential to be a great modern slasher, the film fails in its attempts to go beyond the genre it belongs to.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Ultimately, the movie is more interesting for the shifting power dynamics and relationships among the dwindling group of survivors than for the whodunnit? elements.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Castigates a particularly regrettable aspect of the cultural zeitgeist with the same nastiness that the characters spew at one another. Cringe-inducing? You bet.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: This is a film that plays with your expectations and delivers a drastically different experience. The characters are hard to root for, but the journey progresses in a fascinating way.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: A boffo ending saves the day for anyone still hangin' around and, uh, perhaps that includes some viewers, too . . . Anybody for a sequel? Nobody?
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: To some degree, this movie strives to be purposely annoying and occasionally shocking, reflecting a self-aggrandizing culture in which everyone wants to be the centre of attention.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: Imagine the teens from Euphoria hacking each other to bits. That’s what Bodies Bodies Bodies goes for but in a way that’s somehow less gross and traumatic, and more fun.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Fresh, tense, and funny, 'Bodies, Bodies, Bodies' serves up sharp social satire via a twisted, bloody whodunnit.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: “Bodies Bodies Bodies” may not reinvent the genre, but it offers a fresh and clever spin on a murder mystery.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Horror, particularly of the slasher variety, is often representative of Hollywood’s younger generation....This is also very much true of Bodies Bodies Bodies.... The movie may feel weird to some of us. Is it weird? Or are we just getting older?
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: Is it liberating satire to watch caricature characters get scolded and mutilated because they are privileged and self-obsessed? Or is it unclever “cringe” comedy that punches down at the follies of today’s youth simply because they are different follies?
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: ... Doesn't pull any punches and doesn't make any apologies. It's cutting, mean, and sharp enough to draw blood.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a welcomed, satirical take on Gen Z, affluence, and the whodunit genre, with sharp writing and an all-star cast.
reviews.author: Caitlin Chappell

reviews.text: Even worse than the usual youth-horror junk of this type. A huge step down from the The King of Staten Island for Mr. ex-Kim Kardashian.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Works the time-honored “teen terror” setup but gives it a riotously bloody twist, skewering these young, self-absorbed children of wealth and privilege.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The cast is a who’s-who of people who should be very, very famous in about five years.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The result balances adroitly on the horror/comedy cusp, eliciting lots of nervous, I-shouldn’t-be-finding-this-funny laughter at a recent screening.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: A generational satire in slasher disguise, Bodies may be more clever than credible, but even that gets worked out in the ingenious “oops”-based resolution.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Sure, it's all fun and games until the bodies start piling up - and then it becomes even more fun!
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: ...the cast is on fire - especially Stenberg and Sennott - and the film feels just unique enough to stand out from the crowd.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A sharp, smart horror story that's as much about satirical commentary of wokeness and privilege as it is a genuinely scary movie.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: A super, super smart and wicked whodunit, and the year's sharpest screenplay so far. Rachel Sennott is to die for!
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a gnarly, uncouth, and suitably deceitful breath of fresh horror air.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: An impressively crafted whodunit made for the social media generation, Halina Reijn’s bloody and savage satire “Bodies Bodies Bodies” lives up to the name.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: In the wise words of one Abraham Simpson, “I used to be with it, but then they changed what it was. Now what I’m with isn’t it, and what’s it seems weird and scary to me.”
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: It's like Bunuel’s 'Exterminating Angel' for TikTok kids.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: This is what happens when you try to make a movie that winks knowingly at a done-to-death genre format and don't quite pull it off.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is perhaps the funniest—and almost certainly the meanest—movie I’ve seen this year.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Not an especially intriguing look at a community meltdown, but the movie offers a few electric moments, and DeLappe mostly sticks the landing, which isn't easy in this subgenre.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This pitch-black comedy is a bit too gimmicky, but thanks to its cheeky approach and a terrific ensemble cast, “Bodies Bodies Bodies” works more often than it doesn’t.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: There's plenty of violence amid the confusion and chaos, but it never plants firmly down as a good thriller mystery. The characters are a bit too much, like caricatures. And the reveal is a joke.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a fun comedic mystery thriller with a great young cast and good performances.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: It’s intentionally chaotic and, now and again, surprisingly funny.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: With its runtime of 95 minutes, “Bodies Bodies Bodies” has a cutthroat pace. By the time it’s over, you’ll want to see it play out again.
reviews.author: Danielle Momoh

reviews.text: ‘Bodies Bodies Bodies’ is bloody bloody bloody brilliant.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Devilishly funny satire...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies not only shines a light on another group of extremely talented performers but highlights Halina Reijn as an exciting new voice in filmmaking.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Everyone in the cast, particularly Stenberg, Bakalova and  Lee Pace make "Bodies" a total scream.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: These characters surely deserve their grisly fates, and the ridicule heaped on them, but the movie is neither clever nor sharp enough to make it worth spending ninety minutes in their company.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It’s smart and tense. It displays the tenuous shallowness of people in general and the lack of solid social bounds that define friendship and loyalty. No one knows how to talk to each other without the mask of TedTalks and blinding inebriation.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Halina Reign, not only excels at the capturing the satire in tone, but aptly plays up the murder mystery element as she treats everyone as a suspect as bodies keep popping up.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Maintains an atmosphere of claustrophobia and tension, taking advantage of every second of this entertaining film, giving little respite to the situation and the characters. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Reijin makes good use of these young actors turning on each other which is the core of the story and where the comedy is found. You’ll be laughing at these inept 20-somethings and almost rooting for the killer until the final twist that caps it off .
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The visuals and camera work for this are astonishingly good. The way that the cast each individually seems committed to their respective characters ideals and motivations is felt, and the film took me on a rollercoaster ride making me guess the whole time
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: It's expertly assembled by the filmmakers and a seriously up-for-it cast to freak us out and make us laugh. But even more intriguing is that the movie pushes us to think about the nature of relationships for today's generation of young people.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a great antidote to a summer blockbuster season in which many films didn’t live up to their promise. It does a lot with a little, showcasing its cast and clever story to the utmost.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Don’t mistake 'Bodies Bodies Bodies' as a message movie. It pokes fun at the triviality of its characters just as much as it has fun.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a scathing, brutally funny and bloody riot, but it feels like something that is a sign of this moment in time rather than long-lasting.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Phenomenally written, perfectly cast, and expertly directed, director Halina Reijn's murder mystery is crafted with such magnificence that she leaves Agatha Christie choking in her dust.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Bodies is, at its core, a rather broad comedy, built on a strong and well-picked ensemble.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Some audiences may think the ending is a cheat. Then again, it is a fate these characters might deserve, and a reminder that the modern equivalent of “hell is other people,” is rampant accusations of a best friend being sooooo toxic.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies’ great cast delivers fun in the dark in an easy-going murder mystery.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: The result is a raucous romp that balances suspense with savage humor, making Bodies Bodies Bodies a summer essential.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is the cinematic equivalent of a Twitter argument – but before you run screaming in the other direction, this is a recommendation.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Some of it is bloody entertaining like a classic slasher movie while the rest casts a hilariously biting mirror at the culture that has come to define Instagram and Tik Tok.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: A snarky black comedy with a clever script that expertly blends its slasher murder mystery edge.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies, directed Halina Reijn, takes a handful of familiar tropes and vampirically sucks the stupid fun out of almost all of them.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: ...a hate-watch thriller that scoffs at its characters as much as you do.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: An incredibly fun and unique take on the "murder mystery" genre with a really good twist. I
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: First and foremost and devastatingly a class satire with glass shards tucked in both of its designer jort pockets
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies capably serves up suspense and social satire, despite a few plot holes and an overload of pop culture and slang that will inevitably make this horror movie look very dated.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The screenplay by Sarah DeLappe, from a story by Kristen Roupenian, provides a lot of good twists (including the final reveal) in updating a venerable mystery formula.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is one of those movies that wins you over scene by scene, before sealing the deal with its marvelous, ludicrous ending.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: I loved it. It is so sharp, smart, and such an of-the-moment satire.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It’s a clever take on the one-location slasher with some biting social commentary on Generation Z.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: As it checks off genre tropes, this satirical horror exercise effectively builds some character-driven tension alongside the formulaic mix of laughs and frights.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: As predictable as the film can be in some spots, gotta give kudos to Halina Reijn and her insanely talented all-star cast for making this a wickedly, terrifying, hilarious spin on a premise that clearly had been kept hostage in the 90's until now.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Innocence and guilt slip and slide around as the body count changes and new clues turn up. It tingles the synapses.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Depending on your demographic, Bodies will probably either make you feel seen or utterly obsolete. But it's also just straight-up fun: a black-hearted comedy of manners meets contemporary social nightmare, written in blood and vape smoke.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is at once a keeps-you-guessing whodunit and a sharp cultural critique... This is inventive, fun, and wildly entertaining stuff with more on its mind than fulfilling a standard genre exercise.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The movie doesn’t feel like it’s satirizing the privilege of its characters, or the way that academic- and therapyspeak has crept into everyday language. It just feels like it’s being written by Twitter itself...
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a neon-soaked party that never dies down, a wild murder mystery that will keep the audience guessing and laughing until the very end.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: There is plenty to love about Bodies Bodies Bodies, even if it could’ve sharpened its satirical knives a bit more.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: It’s being billed as a Gen Z horror movie, but Helina Reijn’s movie could better be described as a murder comedy, and a sprightly and inventive one it is.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Its fun comes from watching young people who are supposed to be friends become monstrous. Their attempts to justify their thoughts & actions with “woke” language and motivations is a stitch too. As is watching the story pull the rug out from all of them.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: More of a satire than a horror film, but often quite funny. Rachel Sennott steals every scene.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies should become a cult classic for its fantastic ensemble, hilarious but human send-up of Gen-Z, and delivering suspenseful and brutal horror scenes.
reviews.author: Kyle Logan

reviews.text: Still, while Bodies Bodies Bodies may stumble just before the finish line, it has enough strengths to keep itself from totally imploding.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: The kind of stuff fun summer entertainment should be made of.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: “Bodies Bodies Bodies” is an intentionally vacuous Gen-Z nightmare.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: This is a film that truly reflects the world we're living in, especially the hysteria and paranoia.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It’s the rare film that can match the vapidity and venom of “Bodies Bodies Bodies,” a combination that’s both toxic and entertaining.
reviews.author: David Lewis

reviews.text: In traditional murder mysteries, you don’t much care who croaks, but this was the first occasion on which I found myself actively willing the extinction of every single character, if possible in conspicuous agony. Not one deserves to survive.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is sus.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: “Bodies Bodies Bodies” is stolen by the extraordinarily talented Sennott as Alice. The 26-year-old actress was equally terrific in the subtler, lovely 2020 comedy “Shiva Baby,” but here she’s allowed to totally unleash.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It’s kind of funny and kind of scary, if ultimately neither funny nor scary enough to keep the two modes from canceling each other out.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies contends for the summer's most fun and absorbing film.  It adeptly uses slasher genre tropes to fuel a clever mystery that surprises until the last minute.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: DeLappe’s sharp script brims with delicious dialogue, and Reijn orchestrates it all with a fast pace, maintaining a taut balance of uneasy tension and vicious humor.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies might just be the first great Gen Z thriller. In director Halina Reijn’s film is a razor-sharp satire of a very specific kind of modern privilege.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: A funny comedy, an effective thriller, and a mystery with lots of twists and turns.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Splicing DNA from Heathers, Lord of the Flies, The Invitation, and a host of other influences, Reijn has crafted a shrewd horror comedy that gives the virtual circular firing squads of our modern online lives a real body count.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: In a moment that favors groupthink consensus, trying to figure out who is the "other" in your group really is a deadly game to play. It's also a hell of a lot of fun to watch.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Still, for a screenplay that hates all these characters so much, it’s hard not to want a movie that is willing to go a little nastier with all of them. Grosser kills, perhaps, or meaner moments.
reviews.author: Fran Hoepfner

reviews.text: Bloated with pompous irony. This is a movie perfectly tailored to one of A24’s key demographics: bougie 25-year-olds who value branding over substance.
reviews.author: Lena Wilson

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies makes one wonder if a documentary of its actors playing the eponymous game might be more entertaining.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The film is styled as a critique of Gen Z but it is actually the opposite.  Despite that betrayal, its plot keeps you guessing and the acting is solid, helping it overcome some of its messaging contradictions
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: It may alienate an older audience. But to those it does speak to, it’s a genuinely fun watch that plays on our expectations of the murder mystery genre.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is somewhat exhausting and repetitive but it's also undeniably clever as well.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Wickedly funny, hip and delightfully subversive. A provocative study of the dark side of human nature.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: While Bodies Bodies Bodies doesn’t re-invent the wheel, it’s a timely skewering of youth, wealth, and the perils that come when the wifi connection dies.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: With its darkest depths and its brightest lights, it proves time and time again that it's one of the year's must-see genre films, as existentially frightening as it is riotously funny.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: A good way to kill some time with a few laughs, although many times, it does feel you’re laughing at the characters and their predicament than with them.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: All this mayhem never really adds up to much, as if calling out Gen Z for the folly of their well-intentioned faults was enough. And yet, it is enough, thanks to the film’s very game and hard-working cast.
reviews.author: Mark Keizer

reviews.text: From the sticky, slippery opening frames of “Bodies Bodies Bodies,” director Halina Reijn lets the audience know that we’re in for one silly-smart and deeply self-aware roller-coaster ride.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies struggles at times to deliver a most dangerous game but crushes its extremely online social commentary with piercing sharpness.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Ultimately, the script isn’t as sleek as it needs to be with a board as ambitious as this. The game is a fun one, but you might feel a little cheated once it’s over.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: A fiery and very clever spin on the slasher genre featuring an A+ ensemble that well earns its electrifying mix of thrills and laughs.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: For the most part, this movie is fun fun fun.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Minute-for-minute absorbingly-entertaining Bodies Bodies Bodies  has no weak link among the cast; it's an uproariously and darkly fun generation-Z satire by way of #AmongUs
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Not afraid to get mean and make the audience uncomfortable even while generating laughs, BODIES BODIES BODIES is an entertaining chaotic ride.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: The clever script and charismatic performances make the viewer want to stay to find out how this conflict plays out. The tension continues to ramp up because all of the characters are so volatile. The drama could go anywhere beyond finding the killer.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: This is a razor-sharp social satire that seeks to take Gen Z and its most pernicious personalities to task first and foremost, and on that front, it succeeds wildly.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies leans much more on its humor than its horror, relying on a killer cast and infectious dialogue.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: There ends up being enough organic comedic timing and natural chop on display to charm anyone into a good enough time, if they can see past the parody.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: The dialogue, direction, and smart cast work in tandem to show us down to those depths, and it is that concoction on which the Gen Z parable builds a solid foundation for a unique, darkly funny, and intriguing horror.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: Helina Reijn’s film is as hilarious as it is pointed, with its dialogue distinctly attuned to the Gen Z mindset.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: A thoroughly entertaining, deliciously twisted horror farce that demands to be seen with as big an audience as possible.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: The film is fun. The dialogue is a hoot.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A friggin riot of a slasher comedy for Gen-Z audiences. The deadliest yet most fun falling-out between a group of friends ever.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: At its core, Bodies Bodies Bodies is a detective story without a detective.
reviews.author: Drew Tinnin

reviews.text: If "Bodies Bodies Bodies" doesn't reinvent the slasher genre, it gives it a refreshingly contemporary sense of bite — one that will appeal to horror and dark comedy fans alike.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: In the end, its humours work even better than its frights.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a comedy-thriller for the online generation with as much tension as humor.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: It’s easy to get swept up in the film’s vibe, so why bother resisting? Just sit back and relax, but make sure that your family’s novelty weapons are safely stored before you do so.
reviews.author: Erin Brady

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies offers a great combination of spooks and laughs that is sure to please horror fans.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: It boasts a clever conceit and mostly effective execution, while also offering a refreshing take on the murder mystery.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: The movie feels comfortingly/chillingly familiar, in a blood-and-screams sort of way. And yet, armed with Pete Davidson in a pink sweatsuit and a crackling, Gen Z-baiting script that roasts modern society, it's a rare bird.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Halina Reijn has delivered a tense and audaciously hilarious horror flick. It might not revolutionize the genre, but Bodies Bodies Bodies deliciously leaves us with a taste of fresh blood in our mouths
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies smartly allows its talented cast to dig themselves into a gloriously silly (and bloody) hole, keeping viewers guessing about the resolution until the final minutes.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Its the uproarious image of rich kids without wifi, descending into frothing at the mouth, bloody madness, that makes Reijins Bodies Bodies Bodies an unmistakable Gen Z anthem for blood.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: ...the major problems with Bodies Bodies Bodies is that its not able to keep the momentum going the entire time, and it doesnt know what kind of horror film is wants to be by the end.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: A fun, inverted single location thrill ride, director Halina Reijn creates one rainbow swirl of a good time.
reviews.author: Jenny Nulf

reviews.text: Each actor their own style that brings a varied flavor to the film, which makes the cast is a joy to watch, even if their characters are insufferable.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Using a familiar social deduction game to implode an affluent group of fake friends in the most heinous way makes for a dementedly fun time thats just as mean-spirited with the horror as it is the comedy.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: With a stellar twist ending, a strongly connected cast, and a lot of humor (even if it doesnt all land) Bodies Bodies Bodies is a fun time.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is a true crowd-pleaser destined to takes its place on the mantle with seminal horror-comedy faves like Jennifer's Body and Scream.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Fun, funny, surprising, and occasionally even scary, Bodies Bodies Bodies will definitely scratch the itch for genre film fans looking for something to keep them guessing.
reviews.author: J Hurtado

reviews.text: Like “And Then There Were None” staged by John Cassavetes for the age of Instagram.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Stacks up an entertaining ensemble to deconstruct the slasher genre with witty style. Fun if not entirely killer.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Bodies Bodies Bodies is like a dark, bloody slasher version of Clue with a hint of Mean Girls and Lord of the Flies by way of Scream. Equally funny and suspenseful, an instant classic.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

synopsis: When a group of rich 20-somethings plan a hurricane party at a remote family mansion, a party game goes awry in this fresh and funny look at backstabbing, fake friends, and one party gone very, very wrong.
